records.text: Owens reported that Dr. Deirdre Amaro, whose tenure as Utah's chief medical examiner began July 1, 2024, had resigned from the position.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Her tenure began July 1st of 2024, and now we can exclusively report that Dr. Deidre Amaro has resigned from her position. She's no longer the chief medical examiner of Utah.

verification.notes: Transcript context at 00:01:33 was reviewed. Utah DHHS confirms that Deirdre Amaro began full-time work on July 1, 2024, and a current State of Utah recruitment lists the chief medical examiner position as open until filled. Neither source states that Amaro resigned, and no official resignation notice or independently confirmed report was found. The vacancy is circumstantial, not conclusive proof of resignation, so the resignation claim remains unverifiable rather than false.

records.text: Deirdre Amaro selected Andrew Guajardo as deputy chief medical examiner in 2024.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In 2024, when our chief medical examiner, Dr. Deidre Amaro, began to rule the roost, she decided to select him as her deputy. So he was promoted in 2024 when she got there to the role of deputy chief examiner.

verification.notes: Official records confirm that Deirdre Amaro became Utah's chief medical examiner in 2024 and that Guajardo became Deputy Medical Examiner in 2024. They do not establish that Amaro personally selected or promoted him. The timing and role are confirmed, while the claimed personal selection remains unverified.
